Performs the murti-pratishtha rituals of murtis for BAPS hari mandirs in Pipalav, Verakhadi and Boriya. Blesses the satsang assembly. In a divine, jovial mood. Performs pratishtha arti. Engaged in Thakorji's darshan. Performs murti-pratishtha rituals. Blesses kids who perform a skit. Performs murti-pratishtha rituals for new murtis of BAPS Mandir in Jitodiya. options.headline: During the kirtan aradhana
options.story:
A kirtan in someone else's name

Today, as Mahant Swami Maharaj was going to the second phase of the "Shri Swaminarayan Mahayag", Bhadreshdas Swami asked him, "Have you ever written a kirtan or a shlok or anything like that?"

"Yes, about Bapa. But in someone else's name. Because if I gave it in my own name, they would give it first place," Swamishri said.

Thus, from the very start, a passion for putting others forward. How is this possible without a heart free of envy!

But from his answer they realised Swamishri was speaking of some competition. So the sadhus asked, "Do you remember the words of that kirtan?"

"You remained hidden, no one understood you... something like that!"

"Did you get a place in the competition?"

"Yes, third."

"About how many years ago was this?"

"About twenty years ago."

Thus these talks of the past bore witness to Swamishri's poetic talent.

No complaints, no regrets

After completing the ritual of the mahayag, as Mahant Swami Maharaj was returning to his residence, talk in the car turned to his drawing. In this connection the sadhus asked, "You used to draw pictures of natural beauty on Diwali cards. Have you drawn anything like that on a large canvas?"

"No." Saying this, he himself explained why he drew pictures of natural beauty: "I did not draw Maharaj's murti and so on, because they would come underfoot and be thrown about."

"Did you ever wish to learn painting? Did you learn?"

"No, nothing like that, not even a wish. In school I came first (in drawing)." Then of his own accord, speaking of his studies, he said, "I never came fourth. Everything was done in class itself. No (need to read) books either."

"Swami! If you did some work and did not get credit, did you ever feel regret?"

"Never." Saying this, he laughed and said, "From the start, no one could control me." Then he added, "But I met Yogibapa and stuck to him completely. I was searching for him. After meeting him, everything else became secondary."

Hearing this, the sadhus asked, "Swami! Have you ever felt like complaining?"

"No, never." Saying this, after a while he added, "Just naturally, by nature, no (complaining)."

What a divine and grand life Swamishri's is, free of complaints and regrets!
